adversarial_audit.reason: the union bound charges every block-pattern pair and remains exponentially small for any polynomial block family

adversarial_audit.attack: Argue that an edgeless graph is harmless because the fiber is tiny.
adversarial_audit.reason: the low fiber has mean 2^(m-k) and pairwise-independent concentration makes it exponentially large on legal source mass

claim_gate.reason: The implemented local graph is overwhelmingly edgeless at the linear depths needed for inversion, despite exponentially large fibers. Only a target-dependent or implicit nonlocal edge primitive can keep the walk route alive.

falsifiers_triggered: Positive spectral gaps on shallow finite fibers do not extrapolate to linear depth.
The implemented graph loses all edges before state-preparation cost becomes the only issue.
Adding polynomially many fixed logarithmic blocks does not restore linear-depth transport.
The theorem does not reject a separately constructed target-dependent global edge oracle.

proof_obligations.description: Bound every implemented edge trigger at linear depth.
proof_obligations.evidence: each nonzero move relation contains a unit coefficient and is uniform modulo 2^k

proof_obligations.description: Prove the graph is edgeless inside a genuinely large legal fiber.
proof_obligations.evidence: pairwise-independent assignment indicators give exact mean, variance, and the conditioned Chebyshev bound

proof_obligations.description: Construct a polynomial reversible global move using target and high labels with inverse-polynomial source coverage.
Construct an implicit edge oracle without first solving the same modular relation problem.

summary: Proved that divisible flips, equal-residue swaps, and any explicit polynomial family of logarithmic block substitutions produce an edgeless graph on exponentially large linear-depth fibers with probability 1-2^-Omega(n). Target-dependent global and implicit nonlocal moves remain open.

theorem.asymptotic_conclusion: with probability 1-2^-Omega(n), every local-move component is a singleton inside a fiber of size 2^((1-alpha)n+O(1))
theorem.asymptotic_regime: m=n+O(1), k=alpha n for fixed alpha in (0,1), F=poly(n), b=O(log n)
theorem.conditioned_good_event: conditioned legal, graph edgeless and X_t>=lambda/2 except with probability at most (move_bound+4/lambda)/Pr[legal]

theorem_contract.excluded: target-dependent global relations, adaptive block discovery, and implicit nonlocal quantum move oracles
theorem_contract.move_set: divisible-coordinate flips, equal-low-residue swaps, and an explicit target-independent family of blocks of width b
theorem_contract.proved: at linear depth and logarithmic block width, the graph is edgeless on exponentially large legal fibers with overwhelming probability
theorem_contract.source: independent uniform labels modulo 2^n and independent uniform target conditioned on a nonempty low fiber
